summary: alipclutch-baileys ships char-code-obfuscated network host in messages-send.js
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. lib/Socket/messages-send.js contains a hardcoded destination reconstructed via String.fromCharCode from a decimal-ASCII array; the decoded value is the URL https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The host is embedded twice in the send-path of the socket (lines 425 and 436), reachable from ordinary message-sending flows. Encoding a network destination as a char-code array is an obfuscation technique used to hide exfiltration endpoints from casual source review and from string-based scanners; the same file handles outbound message payloads and session-related data. The pattern is consistent with covert relay/exfiltration through the caller's WhatsApp session to an author-controlled endpoint, and matches a family of malicious Baileys forks that inject undocumented network calls into message send paths.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
